Simulate a cohort with a latent kinetic state

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_mbmm.Rd

Generates the setting the method is built for: a baseline marker shifts the probability of a latent state, participants in that state follow a mechanistic trajectory, and some participants not in it still produce a brief detectable event. A rule that counts any detection as the state therefore mislabels part of the cohort, which is what attenuates a covariate effect and costs power.

Usage

simulate_mbmm(
  n,
  beta_ab = -1,
  prevalence = 0.2,
  p_abortive = 0.4,
  times = c(0, 2, 4, 7, 10, 14, 21),
  lod = 100,
  sigma_obs = 0.5,
  n_pool = 200L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Number of participants.

beta_ab

Covariate effect on the log-odds of the state. Negative means a higher marker lowers the probability.

prevalence

Target marginal prevalence of the state. The gate intercept is solved to hit it against a large reference draw, so the realised prevalence does not drift with n.

p_abortive

Fraction of participants not in the state who still produce a transient detectable event. This is the contamination the method is meant to absorb; at zero, a detection rule is already faithful and there is little for a latent-state model to recover.

times

Visit schedule.

lod

Assay limit of detection.

sigma_obs

Observation noise, \(\log_{10}\) scale.

n_pool

Size of the pre-solved trajectory population drawn from eclipse_design().

seed

Optional seed.

Value

A list with obs (long-format measurements, with censored and lod), truth (one row per participant: the latent z, the covariate x, and the generating parameters), and the alpha that was solved for.

Details

Because the state is generated rather than inferred, the simulation is the one setting in which recovery can be checked directly. It is also the only worked example the package can ship: the analyses in the accompanying manuscript use access-controlled cohorts.

See also

eclipse_design(), trajectory_loglik()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("deSolve", quietly = TRUE)) {
  sim <- simulate_mbmm(n = 12, beta_ab = -1, n_pool = 8, seed = 1)
  table(sim$truth$z)
}
#> 
#>  0 
#> 12
